A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on GSM8k, ToolACE, Guru-Math and MATH, including algorithm comparisons and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds mixed-synchronization results and a GSPO-style comparison using Qwen3-30B-A3B.

M1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds REC-GSPO-IS and REC-GSPO-NoIS, adapting REC to length-normalized sequence probability ratios, sequence-level clipping and sequence-averaged gradients. The existing REC, RED, OPMD and AsymRE procedures remain unchanged; renaming regularization and temperature symbols is not a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8k, Guru-Math, MATH/MATH500 and the same single-turn ToolACE subset for mathematical reasoning and tool use. The added mixed-synchronization and MoE experiments vary training schedules and model configurations within this retained data and task coverage.

E2.justification: GSPO is only discussed as related work in v1. Appendix B.7 of v2 adds an evaluated comparison between REC-GSPO-NoIS and REC-GSPO-IS, the latter implementing GSPO without advantage standardization. The comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a mixed schedule with sync_interval=16 and sync_offset=8. Its new Guru-Math/Qwen3-30B-A3B experiment uses sync_interval=8, clipping parameters 6e-4 and 8e-4, learning rate 2e-6 and batch size 72. These are additional experimental configurations; the original Table 1 settings are retained.

E4.justification: The new Appendix B.7 ablation tests whether sequence-level importance sampling matters for GSPO-style learning on an MoE model. Figure 2 additionally tests the existing clipping/importance-sampling comparison under combined synchronization delay. Earlier clipping-geometry and learning-rate ablations remain; the MATH analysis is relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Running-average smoothing of training rewards remains unchanged and does not constitute uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 2 adds mixed-schedule results supporting faster learning with enlarged clipping bounds. New Figure 12 reports largely overlapping training-reward and clipping-fraction curves for the GSPO-style IS and no-IS variants. The matched earlier result plots are retained; these additions do not establish performance improvements between versions under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds mathematical definitions of the sequence-level probability ratio, clipping mask and update rules. Section 2.2 also explicitly calls the surrogate-loss minimizer unique. The central derivation, bandit counterexample and Appendix A extension remain unchanged, with no new policy-improvement or convergence proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and findings F1-F3 retain the same central contributions: an off-policy interpretation of group-relative REINFORCE, regularization and data-weighting principles, and reinterpretations of GRPO, OPMD and AsymRE. The abstract's added definition of group-relative REINFORCE clarifies existing scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B.4 adds a substantive explanation connecting wider clipping to abandoning the conventional unbiased-gradient/trust-region rationale. Section 4.1 and Appendix B.7 extend the mechanism hypothesis to GSPO, explicitly presenting the evidence as preliminary. Existing limitations concerning convergence guarantees, reward granularity and older-policy training data remain.

D1.justification: Table 1 and Appendix B.7 document the new MoE experiment's hyperparameters and sequence-level implementation. The printed code URL changes from the modelscope organization to agentscope-ai. RED implementation details are moved from Section 4.3 to Appendix B.6, without changing their procedure or fixed weighting temperature.

R1.justification: Section 5 and new Appendix D substantially expand positioning relative to the closest prior methods. v2 acknowledges REBEL's overlap with derivation Steps 1-2, distinguishes CoPG's fixed reference policy, explains micro-batch infrastructure constraints, and relates the framework to mirror descent, NPG and DPO. Additional citations also broaden coverage of recent off-policy methods.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and derivations are retained. v2 clarifies the abstract, condenses experimental setup, separates regularization and temperature notation, combines related work and limitations into Discussions, and moves RED details into Appendix B.6. It also adds acknowledgments and reproducibility, ethics and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: The ICLR format substantially changes typography, text width, figure sizing and caption placement throughout. The scheduling diagram and MATH results move into the appendix; the GSM8k plot gains mixed-setting panels, Figure 12 is added, and Table 1 gains a model column. Several retained plots become considerably smaller.

improvement.justification: The mixed-scheduling and GSPO-style MoE experiments modestly strengthen empirical support, while Appendix D clarifies important relationships to closely related work omitted or treated briefly in v1. These gains outweigh reduced plot readability and Figure 12's inconsistent REC-OneSide versus REC-GSPO naming. The central derivation and existing evidence remain stable, and the additions do not resolve the retained convergence or uncertainty-reporting limitations.
